key_insight: SUPRA-Tex improves single-image 3D generation by separating texture estimation, surface alignment, and completion, which helps preserve fine visual details while producing more consistent 3D materials. The key idea is to avoid blending incompatible multi-view predictions directly and instead align them through a structured pipeline.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of dressing a 3D mesh with relightable materials from a single reference image while preserving faithful texture details. Existing methods often produce artifacts from inconsistent multi-view fusion or lose detail when relying on implicit image-feature conditioning.
method: Decouples the task into visible-material estimation, surface alignment, and observation-guided 3D completion.
Uses super-aligned texture processing to better preserve image details across the 3D surface.
Guides completion with observed views to improve consistency and reduce texture artifacts.
impact: This matters for practitioners building 3D content generation, digital avatars, AR/VR assets, and material editing tools because it offers a more reliable way to generate detailed, relightable 3D textures from minimal input. It can improve both visual fidelity and downstream usability in production pipelines.
